It looks like my SO (and coparent) may be seeing their cancer return. I sure as hell hope this isn't applicable to my situation but it got me thinking about the subject (and remembering how poorly I handled it the first time before finding out their cancer was very treatable and I thought they would die).

My response last time was to cry my eyes out and get really depressed. We found out the good prognosis before I had a chance to come to terms with it.
How do you deal with the impending death of a loved one?

In the past, I have dealt with the death of loved ones...poorly. Usually with drugs and alcohol. I would not recommend this.

Being around others will help. Family, friends, etc. You can't go through something like this alone, so don't even try it.

Ultimately, it's not something you truly "get over". It's like someone shot a hole through your chest. Every day the hole gets a little smaller, and heals a little more. Then one day you hear them brought up in conversation, or see something on the TV, hell you don't have to be thinking about them at all; and that hole rips wide open. You don't get over it, it just hurts a little less each time.

What kind of cancer was/is it?
Hodgkin's lymphoma. As far as cancer goes, pretty treatable and not too bad. Keep in mind, that's the cancer scale so it still really sucks.

This is where faith can be helpful. I'm sorry it came back - but it's sounds treatable? If so don't dwell on it. My husband is going through similar (stage one Cancer in the kidneys). He has to have two partial nephrectomies. He already had the first one. It took two months to recover. We took it day by day (sometimes hour by hour) and had a sense of humor. The poor man was peeing his pants post surgery, if you can't laugh you will just cry. Anyway, he has another surgery early next year. In the meantime we are living life to its fullest. Tonight we went as a family to the beach and stood in the surf to watch the sunset. We spent Monday at the zoo with our toddler daughter who had never been. Two weekends ago we drove to his parents house and just spent the weekend hanging out. We are making the most of our time and loving on each other. That's all you can do. You will drive yourself crazy if you do the "what if" game. Focus on today. Good luck and God bless.

I held my younger brothers hand as he gave his final breath to Ewing Sarcoma. You handle death one day at a time and hope the pain somehow lessens enough to not hate the world and all the pain in it. You handle the pain by becoming more tolerant and understanding of the suffering of those around you. Honestly you just do the best you can.
Plan for the legal and financial stuff. Spend time with them. Enjoy it as much as you can. That's all you can do really.

You should read/listen to the work of Andrew Holecek, a Buddhist teacher who puts a western world spin on all his teachings. He has some excellent day to day lifestyle tips as well as how to transition yourself and a loved one into the next phase of existence. No matter your creed or belief system, he allows you to recall the most basic human essence that permits you to see "behind the viel." He teaches you the value of your thoughts, your presence and shows you that the transition to death is just as beautiful and meaningful as any other life process. Even if it doesn't end in death for your loved one, having the knowledge and tools that he gives you will enrich your lives in ways you didn't know were possible.

Wishing you strength and love and light.
